narrative.overview: Tong Dee Go is a compact mobile toolkit for planning, moving, and feeling safe around Phichai. The interface should feel assembled for a real day out: route cards, map sheets, local service entries, safety notices, and marketplace previews all share one tactile vocabulary rather than becoming separate mini-brands. The system is product-first and Thai-first. It uses familiar mobile controls, tight hierarchy, and clear status language so users can act while walking, riding, or checking a route. Warmth comes from local content, amber cultural cues, and community services, not from generic travel decoration. It explicitly rejects generic tourism templates, placeless blue-and-white polish, government-portal stiffness, and decorative AI sparkle that weakens trust.
keyCharacteristics: Mobile app shell capped at 480px with safe-area aware bottom navigation.
Restrained blue primary system with amber culture and emerald safety accents.
Rounded, thumb-first controls with compact density and soft structural elevation.
Thai-readable Prompt typography, with JetBrains Mono reserved for coordinates, numbers, codes, and technical details.
Local specificity in content, imagery, labels, service names, and route context.

rules.name: The Blue Earns the Tap Rule
rules.body: Tongdee Blue is for action, selection, current location, and focus. Do not spend it on decoration that is not actionable or stateful.

rules.name: The Local Warmth Rule
rules.body: Amber and orange mark culture, food, marketplace, and reward. They should make Phichai feel specific, never turn the whole app into a generic vacation palette.

rules.name: The Safety Is Semantic Rule
rules.body: Emerald means safety, success, verified, or completed. Never use emerald as arbitrary visual variety.

rules.name: The Thai Legibility Rule
rules.body: Thai copy must not be compressed into decorative tracking or ultra-light weights. Use weight and spacing for hierarchy, not letter-spaced novelty.

rules.name: The Mono Has a Job Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono is for facts and coordinates. Do not use it for brand flavor in ordinary labels.

rules.name: The Soft Lift Rule
rules.body: Shadows should feel like mobile affordance, not desktop depth. If a card looks heavier than the bottom nav, the shadow is too strong.

rules.name: The Border First Rule
rules.body: Default containers get a hairline border before they get a shadow. Use elevation when the user must understand stacking or tap priority.

dos: Do preserve `--app-primary` as the action/selection color and route all preset accents through the existing appearance system.
Do design for one-handed mobile use: 42px minimum control height, 16px page gutters, safe-area aware fixed controls, and clear back/escape affordances.
Do make local specificity visible with Phichai place names, service context, route copy, local operators, and cultural detail.
Do pair color with labels or icons for safety, selected, completed, warning, and error states.
Do keep motion short and functional: 150-250ms for state transitions, longer only for map/sheet gestures that track touch.
Do test muted text and placeholders against App Mist and blue-wash surfaces before shipping.
donts: Don't make the app feel like a generic tourism template with interchangeable attraction cards, stock travel language, or placeless blue-and-white polish.
Don't make it feel like a government portal: avoid bureaucratic stiffness, form-heavy dead ends, and overly official tone.
Don't over-index on decorative AI sparkle at the expense of trust, legibility, and real trip utility.

Don't use side-stripe borders (`border-left` or `border-right` greater than 1px) as a card or callout accent. Use full borders, background tint, icon/label structure, or timeline-specific geometry instead.
Don't use gradient text. Tongdee Go uses solid text color, weight, and placement for emphasis.
Don't create nested card stacks. Use spacing, dividers, or a single clear surface.
Don't use arbitrary z-index numbers. Keep layers semantic: dropdown/search results above fields, sticky headers above content, modals above sheets, toast above modal, tooltip above toast.
